newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland will join EMU, but timing remains uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Finland will join EMU, but timing remains uncertain.

text.p: Finland will join the planned third stage of Europe's economic and monetary union -- the only open question is when, Finnish media quoted Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen as saying on Tuesday.
"The euro will be present in Finland and in use in invoicing. At some stage we will also make it our own currency," Lipponen told a briefing, the Finnish news agency STT said.

A national parliament decision due early next year on EMU membership will only be a decision on whether to join in the first wave scheduled for January 1999, he said, adding this would be a difficult choice.

Finland in 1994 approved the Maastricht treaty, including the parts relating to EMU, by ratifying the accession accord to become a member of the European Union from the start of 1995, Lipponen said. According to Maastricht, countries are obliged to join the single currency once they fulfil the EMU convergence criteria.

Finland's public sector deficit and debt according to EMU rules were inside the levels allowed in 1996 and are seen improving further in 1997, which is the year when those who aim to join EMU at the start in 1999 must meet the criteria.
Finland also meets the inflation and interest rate criteria.
The Finnish markka was linked to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) in October 1996, so by end-1998, will not have been in the ERM for the required two years.
But Finland has said it does not expect to be excluded from the starting group because of this, as the markka had been stable long before it joined the mechanism.
EU finance ministers decided last weekend that the first-wave EMU members will be chosen in April or May 1998.
